title: Canary observability bakes and dead-man's signal notes (WIP)
content:
Purpose:
This is a messy working draft that tries to pull together an end-to-end approach to 'observability bakes' during canaries and a concrete 'dead-man's signal' concept for our rollout orchestrations. Goal is to give oncall and stewards a clear short checklist and telemetry taxonomy to make rapid decisions while reducing false positives.

High-level idea (one-liner):
- Treat a canary as a time-boxed ecosystem bake: a small amount of real traffic + synthetic probes + automated health contracts. If the dead-man's signal drops or any critical contract breaks, trigger a fast rollback and an oncall play.

Definitions (working):
- Observability bake: 20-90 minute window during which layered signals are monitored (synthetic + real+model-quality).
- Dead-man's signal: a consolidated heartbeat that must stay within bounds (example: weighted combination of model throughput heartbeat, control-request success rate, APM ingestion heartbeat). If it falls below threshold for X minutes, treat as system-level failure and auto-fallback.
- Bake phases: pre-bake (0m, config + smoke), active-bake (t0..T), stabilization (post-ramp observation).

Why we need this (notes to self):
- LLM features have subtle degradations (semantic drift, hallucination spikes) that don't always show up in classic infra SLOs.
- Noise in user traffic makes single-signal gates brittle — combine several orthogonal signals.

Proposed telemetry taxonomy (priority order):
1) Dead-man's signal (composite, see formula below) [CRITICAL]
2) Infra health: pod/gpu allocation errors, scheduling latencies, queue depth
3) Latency: P50/P90/P95 for token generation and total request time
4) Error rate: 5xx and model-specific failures (decoding errors, OOMs)
5) Quality proxies: hallucination classifier rate, rerank confidence drift, BLEU/RoBERTa-score delta on canned prompts
6) Cost signal: effective cost/tok (surges may indicate runaway generation)
7) User-impact proxies: task completion rate, click-through on generated suggestions (if available)

Dead-man's signal (draft formula):
- DMS = 0.5 * infra_heartbeat + 0.2 * svc_success_rate + 0.15 * apm_ingest_rate + 0.15 * quality_proxy_preserve
- Each term is normalized [0..1] over recent window (5m). Terms:
  - infra_heartbeat: fraction of scheduled inference workers reporting health (no OOM, no crashed processes)
  - svc_success_rate: % of responses not returning 5xx or decode-failure in last 5m
  - apm_ingest_rate: APM ingestion compared to baseline (detects telemetry backpressure)
  - quality_proxy_preserve: relative pass-rate for canned prompt checks (synthetic golden prompts)
- Thresholds (initial): DMS < 0.7 for >3m => escalates auto-fallback; DMS < 0.5 for >1m => immediate cut-to-safe-model.
- Rationale: infra problems get heavier weight because they produce systemic failures. Quality proxies are noisier and weighted lower.

Bake windows and synthetic traffic patterns (examples):
- Micro-canary: 30m active-bake. Real traffic sample 0.5% minimal; synthetic steady-state 10 req/min across 5 golden prompts, plus 1 heavy-case stress prompt per 5m.
- Short smoke: 10m pre-bake focused on startup and routing checks only.
- Long stability bake (for big changes): 90m with progressive ramp from 0.1% -> 5%.

Sample synthetic checks (to be run from canary harness):
- golden_prompt_1 => expected checksum or model answer signatures
- hallucination_probe => measure probability of asserting nonexistent facts (classifier threshold)
- latency_stress_1 => long-context prompt simulating 8k token generation, measures P95 generation latency

Gating rules (concrete examples):
- Block canary from moving to next ramp if any of: DMS < 0.75 for 2m OR latency P95 increased by >40% vs baseline OR hallucination_proxy increase >2x vs baseline.
- If non-critical signal trips (e.g., cost spikes but quality preserved), send notification and continue with human-in-loop approve in 10m.
- Auto-fallback hierarchy: (1) compatible quantized variant with lower throughput but safe fallback, (2) regional fallback, (3) full traffic cut to previous stable model.

Escalation and oncall play (fast path):
1) Alerting: Pager for DMS-critical; Slack alert for degraded non-critical signals.
2) Oncall runbook quick hits: check DMS dashboard -> check synthetic golden prompt logs -> check infra pod restarts/oom logs -> assess primary cause.
3) If DMS <0.5 and infra restarts >3 in 5m => trigger auto fallback to stable model and page infra.
4) If hallucination_proxy >3x but infra healthy => throttle traffic to 10% and page product steward + ML lead.
5) Communications: use template channel #rollouts-status, include: canary id, phase, DMS value, top 3 signals, quick diff vs baseline, action taken.

Sample Slack message template (copyable):
- "[ROLL-##] Canary {canary-id} - DMS=0.48 (P95 latency +66%) -> auto-fallback to stable-2025-02-01. Notifying infra and ML. Investigation in progress. Rolling back now."

Quick checklist for rollout steward (bullet sprint):
- [ ] Confirm canary config matches PR and feature flags
- [ ] Run pre-bake smoke (health checks pass)
- [ ] Kick off active-bake and ensure synthetic probes running
- [ ] Watch DMS and the 3 quality proxies (hallucination, rerank_confidence, task_success)
- [ ] If any gate trips, follow escalation play (above). If manual override needed, document reason.

Observability implementation notes (ops/infra):
- Need a light-weight DMS service that ingests normalized signals (5m buckets) and outputs score + anomaly tag.
- Synthetic probe logs must be stored in a cheap timeseries with full-text capture for first 100 chars (searchable). Consider Elastic + cheap S3 archive.
- Dashboards: small 2x2 panel for steward view: DMS, P95 latency, hallucination proxy, infra restarts. Autorefresh 20s.

False positive sources (lessons learned):
- Telemetry backpressure (APM ingestion lags) triggers DMS drop despite healthy model. Add apm_ingest_rate term so we can differentiate and avoid rollback loops.
- Short-lived transient OOMs during scheduling spikes — add smoothing window to avoid over-reactivity.

Post-bake / postmortem triggers:
- Any auto-fallback must spawn a short postmortem email within 24h with root-cause hypothesis and remediation plan.
- Manual aborts during canary: steward must capture notes in the canary ticket (JIRA ROLL-####).

Open questions / TODOs:
- Q: exact weights for DMS; propose A/B test weightings across two canaries to see which reduces false positives.
- Q: who owns the DMS service? Proposed: infra + observability paired ownership.
- TODO: implement synthetic probe harness as a simple k8s cronjob set and add integration tests (github:repo/infra#PR-412).
- TODO: add a canary id to every synthetic probe log line and index in the dashboard for quick drilldowns.

Related artifacts and references:
- Confluence: CANARY-OBS-OVERVIEW (linked above)
- Jira ticket for household rollout: JIRA:ROLL-7862 (example canary run id inside)
- PR: github:repo/infra#PR-412 (synthetic probe harness sketch)

Notes-to-self (informal):
- Keep initial gates conservative; tune to avoid 3am flame-rollbacks. Start by failing closed primarily on infra issues rather than noisy quality proxies.
- Add short 'explain' text on steward dashboard so new stewards know what DMS actually measures.

End of draft. This is intentionally conversational and incomplete — will iterate after alignment with infra and SRE.

Recent edits:
- 2025-02-10: tightened DMS thresholds and added apm_ingest_rate term (Maya)
- 2024-12-16: initial sketch and bake durations (Maya)
